subject: Operations
title: Internal vs. External Failure
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Internal vs. External Failure.

hook.text: Catching a bad chip before it ships costs $2. Catching it after a customer's laptop dies costs $200.

buildup.text: Internal failures are defects found before delivery—scrap, rework, and retesting inside your facility.

discovery.text: External failures reach the customer—warranty claims, returns, recalls, and the worst cost: lost trust.

twist.text: External failure costs are 10 to 100 times higher than internal ones. The later you catch it, the more it hurts.

climax.text: Toyota's philosophy: stop the line immediately when a defect is found. Catch it now or pay far more later.

punchline.text: Find it early or pay for it forever.

quiz.question: Why are external failure costs so much higher?
options: They include recalls, returns, and lost trust
